stories.headline: Local Referee Blows Whistle So Loud, Geese Reschedule Migration
stories.summary: Witnesses describe the Saturday-morning blast as "decisive" and "honestly a little much."
body: A routine offside call at the U12 fields turned historic Saturday when the center referee produced a whistle blast heard three neighborhoods away.
A flock of Canada geese overhead reportedly circled twice before filing an amended flight plan. "We respect the call," one goose did not say.
Parents on the sideline agreed the call was correct, a first in recorded league history.

stories.headline: Moon Shots Portfolio Spotted Pointing Vaguely Upward
stories.summary: Analysts at the kitchen table urge patience, snacks.
stories.byline: By Bull N. Bear, Markets Editor
body: The household’s most-watched chart drew a crowd of one this morning as its line wiggled with real conviction.
"This is a long-term thing," said a source holding a coffee mug, before checking the chart again four minutes later.

stories.headline: Historic Homework Treaty Signed at Dinner Table
stories.summary: Terms include screen time after math, and dessert after everything.
body: After weeks of negotiations, both parties agreed to a framework that observers call "fragile but promising."
A dispute over whether spelling counts as homework was tabled until Tuesday.

stories.headline: Neighborhood Pothole Gets Its Own Fan Club
stories.summary: Members meet weekly to admire its depth and resilience.
body: What began as a minor nuisance has become a beloved landmark, complete with a hand-painted sign.
City crews say it is on the list. The fan club says it is not going anywhere.

stories.headline: Forecast Calls for Sun, Mountains, and Mild Jacket Indecision
stories.summary: Mornings chilly, afternoons warm, layers recommended.
body: Expect classic fall conditions: a frosty start, a T-shirt lunch, and a scramble for a hoodie by sunset.
There is a 0% chance anyone remembers where they left their gloves.

stories.headline: Library Book Returned 40 Years Late, Fine Waived for Good Story
stories.summary: The book was, fittingly, about time travel.
body: Librarians said the tale of its journey was worth more than the fine.

stories.headline: Moon Requests Daytime Shift, Citing "Feeling Overlooked"
stories.summary: Sun says it is "open to a job share."
stories.byline: By Luna Tick, US and World Desk
body: In a rare public statement, the Moon said it was tired of working nights while the Sun gets all the beach days.
Astronomers say negotiations could take several billion years, which is about average for a committee.

stories.headline: Nation’s Snails Petition for Lower Speed Limits on Sidewalks
stories.summary: Proposed limit: "whatever feels comfortable, honestly."
stories.byline: By Shelly Slowe, US and World Desk
body: A petition signed by thousands of snails arrived this week, delivered by a snail, and is expected to be read by spring.
Skateboarders have called the proposal "a lot."

stories.headline: Every Country Agrees on Best Pizza Topping; Summit Ends Early
stories.summary: Delegates spent the extra time at a bowling alley.
stories.byline: By Marge Herita, US and World Desk
body: In a surprise outcome, all delegations voted for "extra cheese" within the first five minutes.
The pineapple question was politely tabled for future generations.

stories.summary: Shares priced at 25 cents, plus a free cookie.
stories.byline: By Bull N. Bear, Markets Editor
body: The young founders cite strong demand and a very sunny quarter.

stories.headline: Dog Shown Yellow Card for Excessive Celebration
stories.summary: The golden retriever accepted the caution with grace and a tail wag.
body: The pup ran onto the pitch after a goal and refused to leave until it got belly rubs.

stories.headline: Saturday Pancake Summit Ends in Record Stack
stories.summary: Syrup reserves reported critically low.
body: Officials confirmed a stack of eleven before the plate surrendered.

stories.headline: Missing Socks Form Union, Demand Better Dryer Conditions
stories.summary: Spokes-sock says the lint trap "has seen things."
body: A coalition of single socks emerged from behind the dryer Saturday with a list of demands, including gentler spin cycles and reunification with their partners.
Management (Dad) has agreed to talks but refuses to discuss the sock that went missing in 2019.

stories.headline: TV Remote Enters Witness Protection After Couch Incident
stories.summary: Last seen between the cushions, now living under a new name.
stories.byline: By Cush N. Crevice, Irreverent Desk
body: Authorities believe the remote fled after one too many arguments over what to watch.
It is now reportedly going by "The Clicker" and enjoying a quiet life inside a laundry basket.

stories.headline: Household Cat Named CEO, Immediately Schedules Nap
stories.summary: First executive order: all sunbeams belong to the cat.
body: In a unanimous vote of one, the cat assumed leadership of the household Friday.
Shareholders were told to expect "significant restructuring of the couch."

stories.headline: Breezy Weekend Expected to Rearrange Everyone’s Leaves
stories.summary: Your leaves, your neighbor’s yard.
body: Gusts will redistribute leaves fairly, according to no one.
